messages.author: 605c30d4b1d3684f
messages.subject: Plotting trends with ARIMA model
parts:
Hey everybody,

I have yearly time series data that I'm modeling using an ARIMA model (fitted with auto.arima from the forecast package). I'm primarily interested in looking at any trends over the time period of my data and by including time as the "xreg" term I can get a prediction and se of this trend (along with predictions for an intercept and AR terms; no MA terms are needed). I can plot this trend line over the raw data, but would also like to show confidence bands. Anyone know of an easy way to do this with an ARIMA model?

Thanks,
Zack


--
Zack Steel

Landscape Ecologist,
University of California, Davis
zls...@ucdavis.edu

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Plotting trends with ARIMA model
parts:
Zach,

I don’t have experience with the the plot methods in the ARIMA package, but they use base graphics, so you should be able to overlay them with commands like

plot(model)
lines(xvals, prediction + se)
lines(xvals, prediction - se)

Or am I missing something?

Noam

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Plotting trends with ARIMA model
parts: You're right, I was missing something.  I'm just figuring this out myself, but I think what you want is `vcov(model)`, which contains the variance-covariance matrix of all the regression coefficients.  With this you should be able to get the variance of the trend coefficient, and the square root of that should be your standard error.  That is, if the trend term is linear.  I'm not sure how it works with a polynomial trend.
